decision: Do not advance this fixed-policy Linux application pipeline to native held-target implementation now. No engine/application/worker cell achieved at least 20% complete-owner reduction in both opposite-order blocks. This does not reject every preparation architecture or capability omission.
hypothesis: Preparing a complete virgin context/page during current application work can hide repeated renderer startup and protocol initialization. This differs from virgin-V8-only donor preparation.
predeclaredGate: Advance this Linux application direction only if at least one application/engine/worker cell reduces complete-owner time >=20% in both reversed blocks, all original tests pass and every unused preparation retires. Preserve memory/CPU tradeoffs; no public adoption or final admission.
mechanism: One unused fresh context/page is prepared during the current test. Serial control uses the same private fixture adapter without overlap. Every test uses a virgin context; application URLs are loaded only after consumption. Final unused preparations and worker/browser cleanup remain inside the owner interval.

controls.scope: Selected storage/global freshness, no application preloading, and a controlled current-page focus/input/visibility case. Not complete isolation or focus conformance.

retainedCorrections: The copied verifier initially labeled launch policy as separately wrapper-verified although this experiment uses direct browser fixtures. All 32 original runs were reverified with a separate corrected description; test outcomes and measured values are identical. Raw receipts remain retained. Actual process launch policy is not independently admitted.
limitations: Private fixed-policy, trace-off original TodoMVC/SVGOMG corpus. Not a transparent general runner implementation: init scripts before initial page, context/page event ordering, dynamic options and artifacts require native held-target integration. No used page/context reuse.

Eight controls passed, including no current input focus/visibility/event changes during controlled second-page creation. This does not prove equivalent activation, callbacks or scheduling for every application or headed/browser mode.

Pool event counts and reviewed implementation establish expected preparation/consumption. Counts lack per-context identities or explicit discard-close receipts. Zero owned bookkeeping alone is not proof of successful closure: failure-path close errors propagate but ownership is cleared. Passing application runs and outer sampled teardown are bounded evidence, not exhaustive process custody.
Two reversed blocks select engineering direction; they are not population or tail estimates. Sampled CPU/RSS are diagnostic only. Every pair increases sampled peak RSS by about 10–14%.
Complete-owner wall intervals include fixture, runner, preparation, unused work and cleanup; source hashing and application materialization precede these intervals.

Browser executable, ten companion files, driver, runtime and declared source/dependency inputs were bound before and after the application matrix. Direct fixture configuration is verified; actual launch policy and final resource accounting are not independently admitted.

This tests preparation overlap with all capabilities enabled. It is not a new measurement of declarative capability omission, a general runner implementation, a public default optimization or the representative majority-scenario 2x result.
